note.question: Should regulators require maximal AI explanations, or can flexible explanation-depth rules better preserve product quality, competition, and consumer surplus?
note.overview: Two firms sequentially choose AI explanation depth, product quality, and price while consumers sort between them by quality value and explanation preference. A policymaker can constrain firms' explanation choices. The article solves pure-strategy subgame-perfect equilibria and compares strict, flexible, and self-regulatory policies.

source.quote: In search of auto insurance, consumer A receives a (AI-based) quote of $120 along with an expla­ nation: “Your insurance quote differs from the city average of $100 because your neighborhood has 18% greater incidents of theft.” This consumer would be largely satisfied because the neighborhood roughly explains the above-average insurance quote of 20%.
The third component of firms’ products is the explana­ tion that they offer as the reasoning behind their AI’s decision.
AI could also help brands develop successful positioning statements and compelling slo­ gans (Huang and Rust 2021).

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Subject to any policy chosen by the regulator, firms simultaneously select explanation depth in stage 1, product quality in stage 2, and price in stage 3. Consumers then observe product attributes and prices and choose. An extension adds an earlier firm-entry stage and examines voluntary participation under self-regulation. Explanation depth differentiates firms along consumers' preferred-explanation dimension before quality and price competition.
